evidence.claim: 2025 historical National Employment Matrix employment is 170280.8 thousand jobs; wage/salary 160458.6 thousand and unincorporated self-employed 9822.3 thousand. The 2035 column is a projection and is not used as an observed baseline.

evidence.limitations: Date is page last modification. Rounded components differ by 0.1 thousand. Industry jobs include nonphysical work; no physical hours inferred.

evidence.claim: Detailed 2025 industry employment permits facilities/waste split and six deep-cell context denominators.
evidence.locator: Table 2.11, 2025 National Employment Matrix code and Employment 2025 columns
evidence.limitations: Date is page last modification; Exa metadata reports August27 initial vintage. Summary rows overlap child rows. Hospital all-ownership row overlaps state/local government; use private-only row in additive market accounting. Output is gross output in chained2017 dollars, not wages or value added; omitted from market totals.
evidence.acquisition_method: Direct HTTPS and HTML table parser; selected exact rows retained in source_rows

evidence.claim: National Employment Matrix measures jobs, not individual workers; self-employment means unincorporated self-employed.
evidence.limitations: Counts differ from CPS persons and from OEWS coverage; cannot reconcile by silently substituting one for another.

evidence.claim: May2025 OEWS contains 155495730 wage/salary jobs; wages are straight-time gross pay, excluding employer benefit costs and several pay premiums.
evidence.locator: Release introduction; Technical Note Occupational employment and wages; Table1
evidence.limitations: Nonfarm establishment survey excludes most agriculture, self-employed, private household workers and unpaid family workers. Full- and part-time workers included. Annual wage convention using2080 hours is not measured annual hours.

evidence.claim: Selected physically intensive major occupation groups and detailed diagnostic occupations have measured employment/wage rates, not measured physical-work shares.
evidence.limitations: Detailed rows are nested within major groups; never sum both. An occupation name does not identify automatable hours or replaceable employment.

evidence.claim: May2025 OEWS uses2018 SOC and2022 NAICS, six panels November2022–May2025, excludes most agriculture and private households.
evidence.locator: Scope of survey; occupational and industry coding systems
evidence.limitations: Exa retrieved historical technical note; direct historical industry-specific URLs redirected to OES home in this session. No industry occupation estimates fabricated from redirected pages.

evidence.claim: O*NET task-frequency rating values indicate percentage of respondents choosing a frequency category, not percentage of work time.
evidence.limitations: Cannot estimate annual physical hours from task-frequency categories or importance scores.

missingness.publication_date: No dated publication displayed in retrieved source.

evidence.claim: BMW reports Figure02 pilot in Spartanburg during2025 moved >90000 components, supported >30000 X3 and accumulated about1250 operating hours over ten months.
evidence.locator: Section on first pilot at Spartanburg; paragraphs beginning Within ten months and In total
evidence.limitations: Pilot supporting sheet-metal positioning, not autonomous car manufacturing. Operating hours are not calendar exposure or paid hours; intervention, accepted quality and economics undisclosed. Do not infer 10h×5days continuous operation from shift language.

evidence.claim: GXO announced multiyear RaaS deployment of Digit and Arc at SPANX, moving totes from AMRs to conveyors following late2023 proof of concept.

evidence.limitations: Source establishes bounded live operation and arrangement, not fleet counts, throughput, interventions, cash savings, fees or national logistics serviceability.

evidence.locator: Cobots and cleaners: A collaborative force; From routine to responsive
evidence.limitations: Observation period, exact efficiency denominator, sample, robot configuration and controlled comparator undisclosed. Global fleet and UK effect cannot calibrate US labor savings. March19 is page datePublished metadata.

cells.learning_links: BIM-to-execution and as-built feedback supports site coordination; physical/geometric variability limits transfer between projects.
cells.evidence_conclusion: Commercial semi-automated US product and foreign field-case evidence; no measured US market-wide productivity/penetration.

cells.value_chain: Route planning → data capture → defect review → work order → repair → verified asset availability
cells.system_alternatives: Spot/other quadruped with sensors; fixed sensors; aerial drone; wheeled sensor cart; human technician
cells.technical_requirements: Reach/access plus calibrated sensor data quality, repeatable alignment, detection performance and safe communications
cells.economics: Cost per decision-quality inspection includes payload, human review, false positives/negatives, maintenance and repair follow-through. Avoided outage benefit requires causal evidence; mission counts alone insufficient.
cells.pathway_comparison: Utility retains asset/security authority; integrator supplies payload/site mapping. Service entrant can access contracts but cannot assume regulated asset ownership or monetize all avoided outages.
cells.bottlenecks: Operational access, sensor/IQA thresholds, cyber approval, site qualification and unresolved observation-to-action link.
cells.learning_links: Repeated routes improve comparability/anomaly baselines; asset types and failure distributions govern transfer. Inspection-only systems do not establish manipulation capability.
cells.evidence_conclusion: UK operator three-day trial is bounded comparison for US cell; US routine economic evidence missing in atlas and tracked inI/J.

rules: Market families reconcile to wage/salary reference using explicit residuals; self-employment remains unallocated.
Other business residual includes51,52,53,54,55 and contains physical work such as datacenters, laboratories, real-estate maintenance; it is not assumed nonphysical.
Other admin/support=NAICS56 minus5612 minus5617 minus562; temporary-agency work remains here until destination weights available.
M10 uses private healthcare. Public hospitals and schools stay M14; all-ownership hospital deep context is a nonadditive reference.
Market M13 includes private-household employment where national matrix covers it; OEWS excludes private households. Unpaid household care is outside employment accounts, explicit unmeasured activity.
A customer value-chain view must redistribute supplier activity with weights summing to1 including unallocated; no such allocation estimated in this edition.
Source rounding tolerated only to0.1thousand in displayed reconciliation.
No employment×2080 conversion and no task-frequency→time-share conversion.

Physical activity inside residual business sectors
